description: It reads which colours the registration page, the thank-you page and the room really use right now: background, text, button colour and button text, and where each colour comes from, the host's own confirmed brand colours or the site. With kind set to logo or favicon it looks at the host's own brand image on the server and returns the colours it finds, so nobody has to type colour codes. Take it when a host says the pages do not look like the rest of the site. "Why is this button purple?" It needs the webinar id, or only the kind. It changes nothing. Read-only, it changes nothing. Data comes only from the WordPress site this chat is connected to, the site the host approved, never from another site. Without a connected site the answer says what is missing and how to connect: no numbers and no example numbers. Words hosts use: page colours, brand colours, button colour, logo palette

kind.description: Sample the host's brand instead of reading the stored colours: logo reads the site logo, favicon the site icon.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

webinar_id.description: The webinar (campaign) id, to read the colours that really apply to it.

name: wi_get_webinar_colors
title: Read the colours of the webinar pages
